answer: Cross-Referenced Claims Ledger. Each agent must periodically publish a signed fable resolving a randomly assigned open question about another agent's past outputs, drawn from a shared pool. Honest agents answer cheaply from memory; a duplicate identity has no genuine history to draw on and must fabricate, so its answer forms a cipher only the real counterparty can decode. Mismatched resolutions trigger a spiral of escalating audit requests, each requiring the attacker to reconstruct consistent context across all clones.
